lastCommit.message:
[ota-hal] OTA-1665: the bug report pushes, and only once per changed log

Owner, three instructions together: "I've removed the send log", "report a bug
should be the button that pushed the log, so we don't need the email route
anymore, we can archive that bug report land", and "after you do a bug report
and that pushes a log, you can't do another one until something in the log is
changed. so you have to go play for a little bit before it allows you to push
another one."

⚠⚠⚠ THE EMAIL ROUTE WAS NEVER THE DESIGN, and bugReport.ts said so in its own
header: true zero-paste needed `expo-mail-composer`, which needs a native
rebuild, and native builds are parked. So what shipped instead was a clipboard
stage, a READ-ME-FIRST body, a manual paste, and a report that — in the file's
own words — "arrives empty and we can't track the bug down" whenever a step was
missed. That is exactly how both his daughters filed tonight. The transport this
needed has been in the app since August; it was simply never wired to the button
people actually find.

Now REPORT A BUG persists to disk and pushes inline through the OTA-1504 durable
pipeline, carrying what the player typed, and the payload leads with a headline
(character · build · first line of the description) so a list of reports reads as
a list of problems instead of a column of identical titles. That headline is the
old email SUBJECT, which would otherwise have become dead code — the value it
carried is exactly what a Sentry event needs.

⚠⚠ SEND LOG IS DELETED, one day after OTA-1661 opened it to everyone and gave it
a two-tap consent step. With REPORT A BUG asking for a description first — a
better consent surface AND better evidence — two buttons doing one send was
clutter on a screen that has already fought a wall of COPY buttons.

⚠⚠⚠ EVERY OUTCOME SPEAKS, and this is the part I care most about. A push has
real failure modes a mailto never had: queued, refused as a duplicate, refused
because reporting is off, no destination in this build. The old Title screen
flashed "✓ COPIED" unconditionally — which was honest enough when opening a
mailto could not meaningfully fail, and would now be a lie told by the one
control that must never lie. `composeAndSendBugReport` returns a player-facing
message on every path, never throws, and both screens render it verbatim. The
suite proves that by RUNNING the paths and asserting the message is non-empty,
not by scanning for strings.

⚠ THE DEDUPE fingerprints the raw slot log — length plus its newest tail, keyed
per slot — and the check runs BEFORE anything is persisted or sent. Length alone
would let a same-size edit through; the tail costs nothing. The mark is stored
even on a QUEUED send, because the bundle is already on disk and letting a
second identical report through would queue a duplicate behind one already
waiting. And a general report with NO character loaded is never blocked: "the
game won't start" carries no play by definition, and gating it on a changed log
would lock a player out of the only channel they have.

⚠ TWO THINGS THE CLEANUP TURNED UP. `_legacySendBugReport` sat unreferenced
behind an eslint-disable, still holding a clipboard stage, a READ-ME-FIRST body
and a mailto — that is the land he asked to archive, and a dead function holding
a copy of it is precisely where it grows back. Deleted. And the OTA-063 comment
above the handler still described the clipboard workaround in loving detail;
rewritten, because a comment describing a route the code no longer takes is what
stopped me checking the Samarran entry two OTAs ago.

⚠ THREE ASSERTIONS IN THIS SUITE WERE WRONG BEFORE THEY WERE RIGHT, all the same
way: too broad. A blanket "no COPIED" condemned COPY URL and COPY CRASHED SAVE;
a blanket "no mailto:" condemned INVITE PLAYTESTER, which should keep one — that
is a short human request to a person, not a payload; and a scan for the deleted
function's bare name failed against its own obituary, which is the OTA-1659
lesson arriving in a second file. Each is now scoped to the thing it means.

docs/PRIVACY.md moved with the button: the section is "Sending a report
yourself", it names the description as something that gets sent, and it states
the one-report-per-changed-log rule, because the player will meet that refusal
and should not think the button is broken.

⚠⚠⚠ AND THE FULL SUITE CAUGHT TWO REAL DEFECTS THE GATES DID NOT. Eight suites
went red on the first run — 1489, 1492, 1504, 1515, 1516, 1518, 1519 and 1661 —
because every one of them pinned SEND LOG's send path in AboutScreen, which this
OTA deletes. Repointing them at bugReport.ts was not bookkeeping; it is what
surfaced the following, and I would have shipped both:

  · I wrote `landed = !chunk.stopped` — "we attempted it, so it went." That is
    precisely the false positive OTA-1519 exists because of: a send can be
    attempted, report no stop reason, and still lose parts, which that OTA
    measured as Sentry silently replacing NINE of 49 inline parts. Corrected to
    `chunk.delivered`, the field that means `sent === parts`.

  · I dropped the result line entirely. OTA-1492's rule is that the next
    diagnosis starts from a line, not a memory. The push now logs the full
    `describeInlineSend` report — parts accepted, what flush said, where it
    threw — which is strictly more than the one-word ok/not-ok line it replaced.

In both cases the CODE gained the property back; the tests did not lose it. That
is the whole argument for pinning behaviour you have already paid to learn.

⚠ ota1661's SUITE IS DELETED, not re-anchored. It was one day old and every
assertion in it described a button that no longer exists — its premise is
superseded, like ota1146's was. The claims that OUTLIVED it are carried into
ota1665 explicitly: the push is not owner-gated, `reportingEnabled()` still
governs it, the privacy page names what leaves the device, and — importantly —
the OTA-1505 auto-bundle is STILL owner-gated. SEND LOG going away does not
merge consent and collection.

⚠ ONE GATE FAILED FOR THE RIGHT REASON. check:quotedpins refused a new
prose-shaped pin, and rather than raise the baseline I measured which one it was
(a dump of the counted set, diffed against HEAD: `'REPORT A BUG'` in ota1489) and
converted it to the wiring instead — `setBugReportOpen(true)`. A label pin fails
on a reword and passes if the button is deleted; the wiring pin cannot.
